original_question: For a Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), if the squared coefficient of variation c^2 of the event-stationary inter-event times equals 1, does it follow that all modulating Poisson rates lambda_i are equal?
target_in_paper: Section 4 (Conclusion): the unnumbered conjectural open question that for an MMPP, if c^2 = 1, then all lambda_i are equal, with the added remark that the converse is trivial and that the authors do not have a proof beyond order 2. This is narrower than the paper's main numbered conjectures c^2 >= 1 and T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right model class (MMPP), the right statistic (the squared coefficient of variation c^2 of the event-stationary interarrival time), the right equality case c^2 = 1, and the right implication toward equality of the modulation rates lambda_i. It is therefore very close to the paper's actual concluding side conjecture, and it correctly avoids drifting to the broader conjecture c^2 >= 1. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works with an irreducible finite-state MMPP_p, viewed as a MAP with Q = C + D and diagonal D = diag(lambda_1, ..., lambda_p), where lambda_i >= 0. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

The relevant c^2 is specifically c^2 = Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2, where T_1^alpha is the first interarrival time in the event-stationary version of the process. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

The stationarity choice should be explicit: event-stationarity means the initial phase distribution is eta = alpha, where alpha is the stationary distribution of the embedded chain P = (-C)^(-1)D; pi denotes instead the stationary distribution of Q. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

To be paper-faithful, the unresolved scope should be stated: Proposition 3.7 already proves that for MMPP2 one has c^2 = 1 if and only if lambda_1 = lambda_2, so the open part is the extension to arbitrary order, especially p >= 3. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))

The paper phrases the implication as a conjectural conclusion-side remark rather than as one of its numbered conjectures, so the question should not be rewritten as the broader Conjecture 3.8 (c^2 >= 1) or Conjecture 3.9 (the stochastic order). ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
refined_question: Let (eta, C, D) be an irreducible finite-state MMPP_p, with D = diag(lambda_1, ..., lambda_p), Q = C + D the generator of the background CTMC, and let T_1^alpha denote the first interarrival time in the event-stationary regime (eta = alpha, where alpha is the stationary distribution of P = (-C)^(-1)D). Writing c^2 := Var(T_1^alpha) / E[T_1^alpha]^2, does the equality c^2 = 1 force lambda_1 = ... = lambda_p? Proposition 3.7 proves this equivalence for p = 2; does it remain true for arbitrary irreducible MMPP_p, in particular for all p >= 3? ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the paper's main numbered open problems—Conjecture 3.8 (for an irreducible MMPP, c^2 >= 1) or Conjecture 3.9 (T_1^pi >=_st T_1^alpha)—but at a narrower, unnumbered conjectural question raised in the Conclusion. The authors explicitly state there that they conjecture: for an MMPP, if c^2 = 1, then all lambda_i are equal, and they immediately note that they do not have a proof beyond order two. To make the question stand alone, one must import the paper's notation from the Introduction and Section 2: c^2 is the SCV of the event-stationary first interarrival time T_1^alpha, and MMPPs are irreducible MAPs with diagonal D = diag(lambda_i). Proposition 3.7 then supplies the crucial scope restriction: the equivalence is already proved for order 2, so the genuine research question is whether that equality characterization extends to general irreducible MMPPs of higher order. ([cambridge.org](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B037C27C281FB3B22AA591EEB0B5CF99/S1446181122000013a.pdf/stationary-markovian-arrival-processes-results-and-open-problems.pdf))
